payload.headline: Alphabet holds at the 273.1 range floor; cash flow is still the problem

summary.thesis: Sales and margins keep getting better, but free cash flow fell from 73.6B to 19.7B, so 273.1 is a fair price and not a cheap one.
summary.decision: Long-term hold, adding only at 234.35. Swing: wait, with no trade unless the stock closes above 300.07.
summary.act_at: add at 234.35; swing only on a daily close above 300.07

payload.happening: GOOGL fell 2.13% to 273.1. That puts it inside the 271.77–277.07 price zone, and DATA lists no support zones below it. The stock sits below its 20-day (283.05), 50-day (318.24) and 200-day (336.06) averages, and the 20-day and 50-day are falling. The news since the last note is product and policy items: Google's Familiar Faces AI feature now works on Walmart's $35 camera, and Android developers must soon share their address publicly. None of it touches the next big event, the 2027-02-03 earnings report.
payload.business: Demand is strong and getting stronger. Quarterly sales grew 24.65% from a year earlier, up from 21.79% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 33.32% from 32.19%. The weak spot is cash. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 19.7B from 73.6B over twelve months. That is only 4.19% of sales. The filings also show the payoff on new spending is falling: each dollar invested now earns 24¢ a year, against 40¢ three years ago. The 50.03% net margin flatters the picture, because the filings say profit leans on one-off gains. Analysts have cut this year's EPS (earnings per share) estimate by 5.2% in 30 days. They also expect next-year EPS of 14.97, below the trailing 19.06. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 139.0B and liquidity is 265.1B. Today's headlines change sentiment or rules, not the business. The Android address rule is a governance item for developers. The Waymo freeway story is a speculative report, not a filing.

worth.text: The two valuation methods give very different answers. The cash-flow method (DCF, discounted cash flow) starts from today's 19.7B of free cash flow and a 9.9% discount rate. It gives 26.21 / 52.3 / 71.75 per share for the bear / base / bull cases. Even with 30% starting growth it reaches only 79.81. The own-history method uses price-to-sales, the price paid per dollar of sales, at Alphabet's usual 5-year levels. It gives 234.35 / 279.84 / 375.22. At 273.1 the stock sits just under that 279.84 mid, and its price-to-sales sits at the 46.0th percentile of its own 5-year history. Against peers it looks rich: price-to-sales is 7.2 against a peer median of 4.9, and the growth-adjusted ratio versus peers is 1.29. Earnings multiples look modest, at 14.3 trailing and 18.2 on next year's EPS. But trailing profit includes one-off gains. The filings say the price needs about 36% a year growth, against 17% a year delivered over 3 years. The whole gap between the methods comes from the free-cash-flow starting point. The sales method assumes cash will catch up with sales again. The cash-flow method assumes it will not. If the operating margin fell to 24%, even the cash-flow value would drop to 46.44.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the earlier 73.6B as the heavy spending starts paying back. If it stays near 19.7B, the cash-flow values of 52.3 and below are the better guide.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 24.65% year over year in the latest quarter, against 21.79% two quarters ago.
Operating margin improved to 33.32% from 32.19% while sales grew, so the core business is getting more profitable.
Net cash of 139.0B and a price-to-sales at only the 46.0th percentile of its own 5-year history give a cushion.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 19.7B from 73.6B. On that base, the cash-flow method's middle value is only 52.3.
The filings say the price needs about 36% a year growth, against 17% a year delivered over 3 years.
Analysts cut this year's EPS estimate by 5.2% in 30 days, and price-to-sales of 7.2 is above the peer median of 4.9.

levels.what: Today's close, just under the 279.84 own-history mid. That is fair value, not a discount, so it is not a level for new buying.
Bottom of the current price zone. DATA lists no support zones below it, so a close under it leaves no nearby floor before 234.35.
Low end of the own-history range and the add level. It leaves room for free cash flow to stay weak for a while.

longterm.why: Faster sales, rising margins and 139.0B of net cash support holding. A collapse in free cash flow and falling estimates do not justify paying near fair value, so the add level is 234.35.

swing.why: A stop under the 271.77 zone floor sits inside one normal day's move (the ATR, or average true range, is 11.85), and the averages are falling. No trade unless there is a daily close above 300.07, the top of the first resistance zone, with 304.97–311.03 as the next zone overhead.

decision.timing: December options price in about an 8.4% move by 2026-12-18, and February options, which cover the 2027-02-03 report, price in 15.9%. So the 234.35 add can wait for that report's cash-flow figures.

change_mind: The 2027-02-03 report shows trailing free cash flow rising clearly from 19.7B back toward 73.6B: that would support adding nearer the 279.84 own-history mid instead of only at 234.35.
A daily close below 234.35 while free cash flow stays near 19.7B: the cash-flow values (52.3 base) would then matter more than the sales-based range, and the call would move from hold to wait.
Quarterly sales growth drops back below 21.79%, or operating margin falls back below 32.19%: the business half of the hold case would weaken and the call would move to trim.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold with the add at 234.35, because the news since the last note is product and policy only and free cash flow is still 19.7B against 73.6B a year earlier.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
